Zero-inflated negative binomial regression

zinbreg.Rd

Fits a zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression model, similar to pscl::zeroinfl(..., dist = "negbin"). The model is a mixture: with probability \(\pi_i\) observation \(i\) is a structural zero, and with probability \(1 - \pi_i\) it comes from a negative binomial distribution with mean \(\mu_i\) and dispersion \(\theta\), where \(\log \mu_i = x_i^\top \beta + o_i\) and \(\mathrm{logit}\, \pi_i = z_i^\top \gamma\).

Usage

zinbreg(formula, data, offset, control = zinbreg_control())

Arguments

formula

A two-part formula y ~ x1 + x2 | z1 + z2: count-model covariates before the | and zero-model covariates after it. Without |, the same covariates are used in both parts. An offset for the count model can be included as offset(log(exposure)) before the |.

data

A data frame containing the variables in formula.

offset

An optional numeric vector with an offset for the count model, on the log scale.

control

A list of control parameters from zinbreg_control().

Value

An object of class "zinbreg": a list containing

coefficients

A list with components count and zero.

vcov

Variance-covariance matrix of all estimates \((\beta, \gamma, \log\theta)\), from the inverse of the observed information matrix.

theta

Estimated dispersion parameter of the count model.

SE.logtheta

Standard error of \(\log\theta\).

SE.theta

Standard error of \(\theta\), by the delta method: \(\theta \times SE(\log\theta)\).

loglik

Observed-data log-likelihood at the estimates.

loglik_path

Log-likelihood at the start and after every EM iteration (it never decreases).

iterations

Number of EM iterations used.

converged

TRUE if the algorithm converged.

fitted.values

Fitted means \((1 - \pi_i) \mu_i\).

mu

Count-model means \(\mu_i\).

pi

Zero-inflation probabilities \(\pi_i\).

call

The matched call.

together with the response y, the count-model offset, the model frame model, the terms, and the numbers n and df.residual.

Details

The model is fitted by an EM algorithm. The E-step computes the posterior probability that each zero is structural. The M-step fits a logistic regression for \(\gamma\) and a weighted negative binomial regression for \((\beta, \theta)\), both by IRLS (with Newton-Raphson for \(\theta\)). No general-purpose optimizer is used.

Standard errors are obtained by inverting the observed information matrix of the observed-data log-likelihood with respect to \((\beta, \gamma, \log\theta)\) at the estimates. By default its second derivatives are computed analytically; see zinbreg_control().

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 500
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(n), z = rnorm(n))
mu <- exp(1 + 0.5 * d$x)
p <- plogis(-1 + 0.8 * d$z)
d$y <- ifelse(runif(n) < p, 0, rnbinom(n, size = 2, mu = mu))

fit <- zinbreg(y ~ x | z, data = d)
fit$coefficients
#> $count
#> (Intercept)           x 
#>   1.1341602   0.4485549 
#> 
#> $zero
#> (Intercept)           z 
#>  -0.8171633   0.7149913 
#> 
fit$theta
#> [1] 2.05727
fit$iterations
#> [1] 36
